transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you for calling S-Net customer support. My name is Marcus. How can I help you today?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Hi Marcus. I'm having a really annoying issue with my home broadband. Every evening around eight o'clock, the Wi-Fi keeps dropping out on our laptops and phones.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I'm sorry to hear your Wi-Fi is cutting out in the evening, Aaron. I know how disruptive that is. I can certainly look into that for you right now.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Thanks Marcus, it's driving me mad because I attend online evening lectures and I got kicked off twice yesterday.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I can completely understand how frustrating it is to lose your connection during a live lecture, Aaron. Let's get to the bottom of this. Before we begin, may I take your postcode and the first line of your address?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Sure. It's 14 Highfield Avenue, Leeds, LS8 2PX.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you. And for account security, could you please verify your four-digit account security PIN?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes, that's 5 8 2 1.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: That's verified your account, thank you. So what I am hearing is that the Wi-Fi connection drops out intermittently every evening around eight o'clock, specifically on your wireless devices. Have I got that right?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes, that's exactly right. The lights on the front of the router stay solid white, but the Wi-Fi signal vanishes from our phones and laptops.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Got it. Which router model do you currently have set up at home?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: It's the S-Net Hub 4X in the main hallway.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you. And when this happens, do both the two point four gigahertz and five gigahertz frequencies disappear, or is it just the faster network?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: To be honest, we only connect to the main home Wi-Fi name, so I'm not entirely sure which band it's using.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: That makes sense. The Hub 4X combines both frequencies under one name by default. Does anyone in the house connect via an Ethernet cable directly to the back of the hub?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: My desktop PC in the study is plugged into port one with an Ethernet cable, and that stays connected fine. It never drops.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: That is a very helpful clue. If the wired PC stays connected, our external fibre line to your property is healthy, and the issue is isolated to the wireless broadcast.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Right, that's what I suspected as well.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Obviously I need to run a line diagnostic on the hub first before we change any settings. Give me a moment while I pull up your wireless frequency logs.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: No problem, take your time.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you for waiting, Aaron. Looking at the wireless telemetry over the last seven days, your hub's five gigahertz radio is set to auto-channel, and it has been hopping onto Dynamic Frequency Selection channels like channel one hundred and twenty.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: What does that mean in plain English?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: DFS channels share frequencies with weather radar systems. When the hub detects a radar pulse nearby, UK regulations require it to instantly shut down the channel and jump to a clear frequency, which drops all wireless connections for about two minutes.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Oh wow, Leeds Bradford Airport isn't too far from here! That makes total sense why it happens in the evening when flights are active.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Exactly. The radar sweeps cause the five gigahertz radio to vacate the channel immediately. To fix this permanently, we can lock your five gigahertz band to a lower, non-DFS channel such as channel thirty-six.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Will channel thirty-six still give me the full speed of my broadband package?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Yes, absolutely. You're on our Fibre 250 package, and non-DFS channels comfortably carry over four hundred megabits per second across standard room distances.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Brilliant, that sounds like an ideal solution.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Bear with me while I log into your hub's interface remotely and apply that channel lock now.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Okay, I'll wait.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you for your patience, Aaron. I have locked the five gigahertz radio to channel thirty-six with an eighty megahertz channel width, and left your two point four gigahertz radio on channel six.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Great, the white light on the hub just pulsed once and came back solid.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: That's the wireless radio restarting. While the radio initializes, let me check the channel congestion on your two point four gigahertz band. Are any neighbors broadcasting strongly on channel six?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: There are a couple of other networks nearby, but the signal strength for those looks pretty low on my phone.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Channel six looks very clean on my spectral scan here as well, with less than ten percent utilization. That will handle your smart TV and smart plugs nicely.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Good to know. We do have a few smart plugs in the kitchen.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Now let's check your high-speed devices. Could you check your phone or laptop and see if your Wi-Fi has reconnected?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes, my phone has reconnected with full signal bars.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Is the Wi-Fi status symbol showing connected on your laptop as well now after the radio restart?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes, my laptop is connected to S-Net-Home-5G right now.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Excellent. And just to record on our hardware asset log, which router model do you have in your hallway there?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Like I said earlier, it's the Hub 4X.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Of course, thank you for confirming that, Aaron. My apologies for asking again. Now, could you run a quick speed test on your laptop using fast dot com or speedtest dot net so we can ensure throughput is optimal?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Running it now. It's showing two hundred and sixty-two megabits download and fifty megabits upload.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: That is fantastic, Aaron. That is slightly above your guaranteed minimum download speed of two hundred and twenty megabits.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: That is so much better. I'm really relieved that it was just a channel setting and not a faulty cable in the street.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Because it is now fixed to channel thirty-six, the hub will never jump frequencies when local radar sweeps occur, so your evening lecture drop-outs are resolved.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: That completely sorts it out. Do I need to restart the router manually every week or anything like that?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: No, there's no need to power cycle it regularly. The Hub 4X performs automatic background maintenance reboots during the early hours of the morning once a month.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Understood. And will this channel setting stay in place if there's a power cut?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Will the hub remember channel thirty-six after a power outage?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Yes, the manual channel assignment is saved directly to the hub's non-volatile flash memory, so it will persist across reboots and power cuts.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Perfect. That gives me great peace of mind for my seminar tomorrow evening.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: You can also use the My S-Net mobile app to monitor connected devices and run quick in-home Wi-Fi health tests whenever you like.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: I didn't know the app could do that, I'll definitely download it.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: It's available on both the Apple App Store and Google Play Store. It even shows signal strength in each room.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: That's really handy for checking the back bedroom. Thanks Marcus.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: You are very welcome, Aaron. Is there anything else with your S-Net broadband, television, or mobile that I can assist you with today?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: No, that was everything I needed help with today. Everything is crystal clear.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I'm glad we could resolve the Wi-Fi dropping issue for you today, Aaron.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Thanks again for your time and expertise.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: It was my pleasure. Thank you for choosing S-Net, Aaron, and have a wonderful evening.
